official.tuition_coverage_note: The award covers tuition expenses and student living expenses. It does not cover, for example, the cost of international travel, clothing, furniture, or living expenses for family members.

official.citizenship_residency: Available in Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania and Uganda. official.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme is an opportunity for outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing their studies to pursue postgraduate education. Established in 1969, it has supported more than 1,500 students to date.
official.program_type: Private foundation scholarship, half grant and half loan, for postgraduate study

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a fully funded scholarship in the way most catalogues present it: the AKF ISP is half grant and half loan, so 50 percent of the award is repayable with a service charge and a guarantor must co-sign the agreement. Repayment begins six months after graduation, after termination of studies, or after support is withdrawn for failing to meet the academic standards expected of ISP students. The award covers tuition and student living expenses but explicitly excludes international travel, clothing, furniture and family living costs, so your own budget has to absorb the flight home and settling-in items. Treat it as a resource of last resort and arrive with a credible multi-source funding plan covering every year, because the Foundation states that this is exactly what it expects to see.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-year Master's or PhD applicants from the listed eligible countries with strong academic records, genuine need, and a documented plan to fund the rest of their study.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country of eligibility first, using the AKDN eligibility chatbot, because the country list is restrictive and excludes study in the United Kingdom or Russia
Secure admission to a reputable postgraduate institution before or alongside the application, since evidence of admission is required
Build a written multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study, not just year one
Identify a guarantor who is willing to co-sign the award agreement before you accept
Model the repayable 50 percent plus service charge as a post-graduation liability, with repayment starting six months after graduation
common_rejection_risks: Applying after enrolment has already begun, since only students starting the first year of a postgraduate programme are eligible
Presenting the AKF ISP as the sole source of funding, when the Foundation calls it a resource of last resort
Applying for a part-time programme or short-term course, which are not considered
Planning to study in the United Kingdom or Russia, which are excluded at present
For PhD applicants, assuming support runs for the whole degree when it covers only the first two years
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel, clothing, furniture and living expenses for family members are explicitly excluded. PhD applicants must find alternative funding from year three onwards.
document_audit: The guarantor co-signature is a condition of the award agreement, so a missing or unwilling guarantor blocks the award rather than being an administrative afterthought
Local and regional universities and distance learning programmes are acceptable only if course quality is maintained, so the institution's standing matters
Evidence of admission must be to the first year of a postgraduate programme; prior postgraduate enrolment disqualifies the applicant
Ongoing financial need and good academic standing must be demonstrated during the programme to keep the award
alerts: The 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next opens in early 2027, so applications sent to a local contact now will not be considered
Repayment of the loan component, including the service charge, starts six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support for academic reasons
There is no central deadline; timing is controlled by the local AKF contact, so contact your country team before the cycle opens rather than after
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Verify eligibility through the AKDN chatbot, contact the local AKF team in your eligible country, submit the application with evidence of admission, need and a multi-source funding plan during the open cycle, then complete the guarantor co-signature if selected.
